chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Driving to Oklahoma City
summary: She drove John's old Chevrolet 600 miles from Memphis to Oklahoma City with his mother, fixing tyres herself thanks to Roland Mayfield's training.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I see. So you led the band and finished those up? Then was that when you went to Oklahoma City?

Yes, drove to Oklahoma City, changed tires and everything. His mother was with me. A little old car that John had, a Chevrolet, looked like a bathtub. I have a picture of it now and I laugh about it. I drove from Memphis to Oklahoma.
How long did it take you, do you know?
I don't remember. I know we had flat tires and everything on the way.

Oh, I did. I changed the tires and I'd fix them up. Roland Mayfield, you know, the man who used to pick me up in Pittsburgh, taught me how to drive and how to fix cars and everything. My brother-in-law helped and if anything was wrong with any of those cars I could fix it myself. His mother was with me. It was like being on a desert, all the turtle-back roads, sand, dirt roads, you know. So we finally made it there and got in all right. See Roland taught me how to - I used to race when I was 10 or 12 years old. He taught me how to race and all that, do tricks in the car.
